## 4. Assumptions and limits

*Numbers carry markers and are verified by `check_prose.py`; tables are generated by `pp_limits.py`, `pp_strata.py`, `pp_wcurse.py` (see the Makefile).*

### 4.1 The same 168 groups, re-split
Every experiment of every branch draws from one labelled data set: 168⟦data.pair_groups⟧ pair groups (521⟦data.judgments⟧ judgments of which 51%⟦data.decisive_share⟧ are decisive, 14%⟦data.tie_share⟧ ties and 35%⟦data.not_apply_share⟧ "not applicable"), 284⟦data.images⟧ distinct frames of 3⟦data.sessions⟧ growth sessions (111⟦data.session1_images⟧, 108⟦data.session2_images⟧ and 65⟦data.session3_images⟧ frames). The comparison graph (frames as nodes, labelled groups as edges) falls into 117⟦data.components⟧ connected components. A "new seed" changes the random split into initial / pool / validation / test groups, the random label draws and the training randomness; it never adds data. The held-out set of one seed has on average 63.5⟦test.n_decisive.A⟧ (split A) or 53.2⟦test.n_decisive.B⟧ (split B) decisive judgments. Consequences: (a) Wilcoxon p-values and bootstrap intervals over seeds describe the variability of splits, label draws and training, **not** sampling of new growth runs, so they are optimistic; (b) a pre-registered confirmation on unused seeds protects against selection on the development seeds, not against properties of these 168 groups; (c) per-type numbers, in particular HTR, rest on a handful of held-out judgments per seed and split.

### 4.2 Dense, near-duplicate frames
The frames are a nearly continuous sampling of three runs. Distances below are 1 − cosine similarity of the centred, normalised frozen SimCLR features (the geometry of the graph). The median distance of a held-out judgment's farther image to its nearest training image is 0.020⟦nov.b10.nov_train_max.median⟧ at budget 10 and 0.004⟦nov.b60.nov_train_max.median⟧ at budget 60; the nearer image is at 0.001⟦nov.b10.nov_train_min.median⟧ and 0.000⟦nov.b60.nov_train_min.median⟧ (median), and 97%⟦nov.b60.nov_train_min.share_le_001⟧ of held-out judgments have an image within 0.01⟦-⟧ of a training image at budget 60. For scale, the distance between two reference images of the same type has median 0.129⟦ref.same_type.median⟧, between different types 0.584⟦ref.diff_type.median⟧. So test frames are not "new situations" but neighbours of training frames, which is exactly what a smoothness regulariser on a kNN graph can exploit. Strict de-duplication of the labelled data is not possible (red-team audit 2: at distance ≤ 0.002⟦-⟧ only a minority of the candidate pool survives).

### 4.3 Anchor-near versus anchor-far judgments (secondary endpoint of every study)
The learners use typed ideal images ("anchors"); many of them are near-copies of trajectory frames. Of the 2359⟦af.n_total⟧ held-out judgments of the red-team development block, 47%⟦af.anc_all_min.near<=0.001⟧ involve an image within 0.001⟦-⟧ of some typed anchor (39%⟦af.anc_ref_min.near<=0.001⟧ for the reference images alone), 22%⟦af.anc_all_min.far>0.03⟧ have both images farther than 0.03⟦-⟧ from every anchor ("anchor-far"; 29%⟦af.anc_ref_min.far>0.03⟧ for references alone). The **anchor-far secondary endpoint** is the AUC / accuracy computed on these judgments only. Table (AUC gain by stratum; development block, 20⟦-⟧ seeds, red-team per-judgment predictions; split A / split B; the last two rows use budgets 20 and 40 only):

Reading, honestly (red-team **confirmation block**, 35⟦-⟧ unused seeds; the development block, 20⟦-⟧ seeds, is in the table as well): (i) the gain of the best learner over the tuned graph-free control is clearly positive in anchor-near judgments (+0.035⟦cl.R1.conf.A.near<=0.001.auc.gain⟧ / +0.037⟦cl.R1.conf.B.near<=0.001.auc.gain⟧ AUC), about zero in the bands between (0.001⟦-⟧ to 0.01⟦-⟧: +0.001⟦cl.R1.conf.A.0.001-0.01.auc.gain⟧ / −0.000⟦cl.R1.conf.B.0.001-0.01.auc.gain⟧; 0.01⟦-⟧ to 0.03⟦-⟧: −0.002⟦cl.R1.conf.A.0.01-0.03.auc.gain⟧ / −0.002⟦cl.R1.conf.B.0.01-0.03.auc.gain⟧) and positive again in anchor-far judgments (>0.03⟦-⟧: +0.019⟦cl.R1.conf.A.far>0.03.auc.gain⟧ / +0.013⟦cl.R1.conf.B.far>0.03.auc.gain⟧ AUC with intervals above or touching zero, accuracy +0.029⟦cl.R1.conf.A.far>0.03.acc.gain⟧ / +0.029⟦cl.R1.conf.B.far>0.03.acc.gain⟧). With the red team's own threshold 0.01⟦-⟧ the far stratum mixes the empty middle band into it and the AUC gain is +0.003⟦cl.R1.conf.A.far>0.01 (red-team threshold).auc.gain⟧ / +0.001⟦cl.R1.conf.B.far>0.01 (red-team threshold).auc.gain⟧: **the anchor-far verdict depends on the threshold**, and only about 12⟦-⟧ judgments per (seed, budget, draw) cell lie beyond 0.03⟦-⟧, so this stratum is noisy; the red team's frozen RT1 rule (threshold 0.01⟦-⟧, one Holm family with its de-duplication and time-blocked tests) is its to report; (ii) by component: the Laplacian regulariser's gain over aw8_all stays positive anchor-far (>0.03⟦-⟧: +0.013⟦st.conf.lap3_k10.aw8_all.A.far>0.03.auc.gain⟧ / +0.027⟦st.conf.lap3_k10.aw8_all.B.far>0.03.auc.gain⟧; >0.01⟦-⟧: +0.009⟦st.conf.lap3_k10.aw8_all.A.far>0.01 (red-team threshold).auc.gain⟧ / +0.010⟦st.conf.lap3_k10.aw8_all.B.far>0.01 (red-team threshold).auc.gain⟧), whereas the extra gain of the four-fold schedule over lap3_k10 sits in anchor-near judgments (+0.021⟦st.conf.lap3_k10_st4.lap3_k10.A.near<=0.001.auc.gain⟧ / +0.018⟦st.conf.lap3_k10_st4.lap3_k10.B.near<=0.001.auc.gain⟧) and is not resolved anchor-far (+0.012⟦st.conf.lap3_k10_st4.lap3_k10.A.far>0.03.auc.gain⟧ / −0.001⟦st.conf.lap3_k10_st4.lap3_k10.B.far>0.03.auc.gain⟧ at >0.03⟦-⟧; −0.003⟦st.conf.lap3_k10_st4.lap3_k10.A.far>0.01 (red-team threshold).auc.gain⟧ / −0.006⟦st.conf.lap3_k10_st4.lap3_k10.B.far>0.01 (red-team threshold).auc.gain⟧ at >0.01⟦-⟧); (iii) the earlier anchor-weight gain (aw8_all over the default head) is as large in anchor-far judgments (+0.020⟦st.conf.aw8_all.baseline.A.far>0.03.auc.gain⟧ / +0.034⟦st.conf.aw8_all.baseline.B.far>0.03.auc.gain⟧) as anywhere, so it is not an anchor-copy artefact; (iv) a time-blocked evaluation (whole 100⟦-⟧-frame blocks of a run held out, 25⟦-⟧-frame buffer removed from training groups, candidate pool and graph; red-team audit 3, development block) keeps the gain: AUC +0.026⟦cl.R3.auc.gain⟧ [+0.021⟦cl.R3.auc.lo⟧, +0.031⟦cl.R3.auc.hi⟧], accuracy +0.012⟦cl.R3.acc.gain⟧ [+0.004⟦cl.R3.acc.lo⟧, +0.020⟦cl.R3.acc.hi⟧] over the tuned graph-free control, and +0.114⟦cl.R3c.auc.gain⟧ AUC over the shuffled-graph control (table `tables/redteam_extra.md`); this split still stays inside the three known runs. The strata of the red-team confirmation block are added to `tables/strata.csv` automatically once all of its per-judgment files exist (they did when this package was built).
**Only the red team's learners have an anchor-far version**: the confirmation cells of the individual studies store aggregated metrics only, so the claims of the other branches (GM, GE, selection) have no anchor-far check; re-running them with per-judgment output is listed in `GPU_TASKS_paper_package.md`.

### 4.4 Tuned on development seeds (winner's curse)
Every frozen candidate was chosen on development seeds that share the 168 groups with the confirmation seeds: the anchor weight 8⟦-⟧, lambda 3⟦-⟧ with k 10⟦-⟧, the factor 4⟦-⟧ and the graph-free control's schedule (steps ×2⟦-⟧, learning rate ×0.5⟦-⟧; chosen on 12⟦-⟧ to 20⟦-⟧ development seeds). The table compares the development gain with the gain on the pre-registered confirmation seeds for the same learner pair (ratio = confirmation / development; 40⟦wc.n_cells⟧ cells; median 0.93⟦wc.ratio_median⟧, range 0.50⟦wc.ratio_min⟧ to 2.42⟦wc.ratio_max⟧, 65%⟦wc.share_below_1⟧ of the cells below 1⟦-⟧):

{{INCLUDE:tables/winners_curse.md}}

The confirmation, not the development number, is the evidence; the typical shrinkage is small but single cells lose up to half of the development effect. The "tuned graph-free control" is tuned on one dimension only (steps and learning rate); other graph-free regularisers were tried only in development (consistency regularisation comes within −0.005⟦cl.D2.A.auc.gain⟧ / −0.007⟦cl.D2.B.auc.gain⟧ AUC of the best learner).

### 4.5 Other limits
- **Endpoint.** All learner and selection claims are about held-out preference judgments. On the paper's own endpoint (type accuracy of 28 ideal images) no learner or graph method beats 1-NN in a way attributable to the learner (claim G6); that endpoint cannot rank methods.
- **Controls are weak or narrow.** A shuffled graph is far worse than no graph (claim G3), so beating it is a low bar; the noisy-graph and non-graph controls are more informative but exist only for part of the claims.
- **Harsh splits.** The held-out-run and held-out-temperature tests use fixed test sets (50⟦-⟧ and 26⟦-⟧ judgments); the second confirmation block reuses the same test judgments, and test-group bootstrap intervals include zero in 7⟦cl.G5.tgb.n_ci_include_zero_of_8⟧ of 8⟦-⟧ cases.
- **Frozen features, CPU only.** Nothing was tested with an end-to-end fine-tuned encoder; the learner results are for a head on cached SimCLR features.
- **Selection** was examined single-shot from the initial model; sequential rounds with the best learner and selection from a cold start under `lap3_k10_st4` were not examined.
- **Branches not in the package yet.** Studies of other conversations that had no result files when this package was built (representation, anchor exchange, temporal graph) and the red team's confirmation block are not included; see the README for how to add them.
